policies.name: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) system
policies.summary: One of the world's earliest mandatory EPR programmes, requiring producers to take back and recycle packaging, batteries, tyres, and electronics.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Korea

policies.name: Disposable cup deposit pilot
policies.summary: Pilot programme in Jeju and Sejong charges a refundable deposit on coffee-shop disposable cups; under nationwide review for expansion.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Korea

newsFeed.headline: Seoul cafes pilot reusable cup-share scheme as disposable use rebounds
newsFeed.summary: After post-pandemic disposable-cup use rebounded, Seoul partnered with chains on a borrow-and-return reusable cup network.

wooby.headline: South Korea recycles more than 7 in 10 plastic items — and is testing reusable coffee cups.
wooby.narrative: Wooby thinks South Korea is one of the recycling champions. Some cities are even testing reusable coffee cups you borrow and bring back. Wooby would love a coffee. (No, Wooby is a whale.)
